title: THE BIG 6 · GAUNTLET + THE MISSING MILE
vibe: YELLOW-GREEN · You bought back 20 minutes, so today gets both halves. First the gauntlet: one bell, six stations, cycled without stopping until the clock runs out. Then the only thing in this entire program you have never actually done — a genuinely easy, steady Zone 2 run. The gauntlet is where you go hard. The run is where you prove you can hold back. Both count.
why: The 30-minute version of today had no treadmill in it, and the only reason was the clock. With 50 minutes that constraint is gone, so the session gets its second half back — and I'm spending it on the single biggest hole in your log. You have run 2 miles Thursday and 2 miles Friday, you set a 2-mile PR of 15:06 last week, you have run a fartlek, a tempo and a 12% climb. What you have NEVER run, not once in this entire program, is a true steady Zone 2. It has been flagged as the standing gap since the middle of July and it has been skipped every single time because every day ended up being a day to push. Today is the day it actually fits: you are doing 18 minutes of near-continuous work with a 40 lb bell on 6 hours of sleep, and the correct partner to that is easy aerobic running, not a third flat two-miler at tempo pace. The strength side stays exactly as intense as you asked — in fact the gauntlet gets two extra minutes and a fifth-round stretch target. What changed is that the extra time went to filling a hole rather than to piling on more of what you already do well. On the run itself, be clear-eyed about what the challenge is: for you the hard part of Zone 2 is not the effort, it is the restraint. Your habitual pace band is 7:37 to 7:56 because that IS your easy, and you have almost never run genuinely slower on purpose. Holding 6.0 to 6.5 on the console for 18 minutes without letting it drift is a discipline exercise, and that is precisely why it has never happened. One more note so it does not get lost: the last three runs in your log have all been flat — the fartlek Tuesday, then Thursday and Friday. INCLINE is due, and it is queued for your next run day. It is not in today because today already has 18 minutes of gauntlet in front of it and stacking a 12% climb on top of that on short sleep is not a trade worth making. Warm-up is Moves Method Day A, aimed straight at the stiffness you reported.

blocks.title: MOBILITY WARM-UP · SHOULDERS, SPINE + HAMSTRINGS
blocks.meta: ~6 min · Moves Method Day A · aimed directly at the stiffness you reported · includes a rehearsal lap of the gauntlet
blocks.text: You said stiff, not sore, so this is about restoring range before you press and get up under a 40 lb bell — not about recovery. Move continuously, don't linger: shoulder dislocates with a towel or broomstick x12 · thoracic rotations 8/side · Jefferson curl, slow, one vertebra at a time x5 · single-leg goodmorning 8/side · hamstring walkouts x6 · active pigeon 30s/side · horse-stance squat hold 30s · wrist rocks and circles x15 each direction (you're about to rack and press a bell repeatedly, the wrists need it) · deep squat hold 30s with your elbows pushing your knees out · ankle rocks 10/side. Finish with the rehearsal: one full light lap of all six gauntlet stations using the 16 kg — two reps of each, just to wake the patterns up. That rehearsal lap is not optional today; the first round of a gauntlet is where technique breaks when you're stiff.

blocks.title: BLOCK 1 · THE BIG 6 (six-station gauntlet)
blocks.meta: ~18 min clock · ONE 40 lb bell for everything · six stations cycled continuously · GREEN target 4 rounds · 5 is a big day · YELLOW 3
blocks.format: CIRCUIT / GAUNTLET · 18-min clock · move station to station with minimal rest · rest 45–60s only at the END of a full round · count ROUNDS
blocks.workRest: Six stations, one bell, in this order, back to back: goblet squat, swing, clean, press, snatch, get-up. You do not rest between stations — the transition IS the rest, which is the whole point of a gauntlet and the thing your chains and EMOMs never trained. Rest 45 to 60 seconds only after you finish all six, then start the next round. Four full rounds in 18 minutes is the target; five is a genuinely big day on 6 hours of sleep. Treat round one as your real warm-up and don't chase the clock until round two. AUTOREGULATE: if your shoulder or T-spine still feels stiff when you get to the snatch station in round one, run the snatch with the 16 kg instead of the 40 for the rest of the session — that's a smart call, not a scaled one.

items.name: 1 · Goblet Squat ×10
items.detail: 40 lb · bell at the chest, elbows inside the knees, sit straight down to full depth and drive up. Your squat pattern hasn't been loaded since the Olympic chain five days ago. Chest tall, heels down, no rushing the bottom.

items.name: 2 · Two-Hand Swing ×15
items.detail: 40 lb · hike hard, snap the hips, float to chest height. This is your engine station and your grip station — the HYROX material is blunt that the swing is the single best builder of grip endurance under repeated load, which is exactly the quality that failed you on Monday's chain. Fifteen crisp reps, hips not knees.

items.name: 3 · Clean ×5/side
items.detail: 40 lb · single-arm. Hike back between the legs and snap it into the rack — a hinge that finishes in the rack, not a curl. Let the bell roll around the forearm, don't bang the wrist. Five each side, switching hands without setting it down if you can.

items.name: 4 · Strict Press ×5/side
items.detail: 40 lb · from the rack, no leg drive, no push press. Ribs down, glutes tight, press to a full lockout with the bicep by the ear. Pressing hasn't been loaded since the 27th. If round 3 or 4 turns into a grind, that's fine — grind it, just don't turn it into a push press.

items.name: 5 · Snatch ×5/side
items.detail: 40 lb (or 16 kg — see the autoregulation note) · one motion from the hike to a locked-out overhead punch. Don't let it flop onto the wrist; punch through at the top. Five each side. This is the power station, so keep the reps fast even as the round gets long.

items.name: 6 · Get-Up ×1/side
items.detail: 40 lb · one full get-up each side, floor to standing and back down, no rushing. This is the deliberate brake in the round — a slow, technical, full-body movement dropped in right when you're most out of breath. Eyes on the bell the whole way up. Then rest 45 to 60 seconds and start round two.

blocks.text: This is a shape you have never run. Chains, ladders, EMOMs, supersets, isolation work, carries — but never a true six-station gauntlet cycled continuously, which is the format HYROX and CrossFit programming leans on precisely because it trains the transitions between patterns rather than any one pattern in isolation. One round covers every movement family you own: squat, hinge, pull, push, ballistic, get-up. That's why it's the right answer to four days without a bell. The single 40 is deliberate — dense and continuous beats heavy and grinding on six hours of sleep, and one implement means zero setup time between stations. Count your rounds, and notice which station is the one that starts falling apart. Four rounds means the next gauntlet gets a seventh station or a heavier tool.

blocks.title: BLOCK 2 · THE MISSING MILE (true steady Zone 2)
blocks.meta: ~18 min · treadmill · 6.0–6.5 console, FLAT · conversational the entire way · the one quality this log has never contained
blocks.format: STEADY ZONE 2 · 18 min continuous · one speed, no surges, no drift · roughly 1.9–2.0 miles
blocks.workRest: Set the belt to 6.0, zero incline, and hold it. If 6.0 genuinely feels like shuffling after five minutes, go to 6.3, and 6.5 is the ceiling — do not touch it again after that. The test is not the speed, it's the DRIFT: if you find yourself at 7.0 in minute twelve because it felt too easy, the session failed. Breathe through your nose the whole way, or hold a full sentence out loud without gasping. That's the gauge, not the number on the console. Cadence 168 to 172 as always — at a slower speed that means shorter, quicker, lighter steps, which is exactly the point. Eighteen minutes, one pace, done.

items.name: 0:00–5:00 · Settle in
items.detail: 6.0 console, 0% incline (~9:30 per mile on your watch). It will feel absurdly slow for the first few minutes. That is the correct feeling and it is not a sign the prescription is wrong. Let your heart rate come down out of the gauntlet and find a rhythm.

items.name: 5:00–15:00 · Hold it
items.detail: 6.0 to 6.5, whatever is genuinely conversational. This is the block that matters. Nose breathing, relaxed shoulders, quick light feet. You will want to speed up. Don't. Every other run you have logged in the last three weeks has been at or above tempo — this is the aerobic work underneath all of that, and it is the only thing missing.

items.name: 15:00–18:00 · Finish honest
items.detail: Same speed to the end. No kick, no negative split, no finishing fast because you feel good. Finishing this run feeling like you could have done another twenty minutes IS the successful outcome.

blocks.text: This is the missing piece and it has been missing since the program started. Your log has a 15:06 two-mile PR, a Mona fartlek with 30-second reps at 9.0, a 12% incline pyramid that hit HR 160, and roughly a dozen flat two-milers at 7:37 to 7:56. What it does not have, anywhere, is one genuinely easy steady aerobic run. Your own running history file says it plainly: your pace band is narrow because 7:37 to 7:56 IS your easy, and you have a 3 to 4 mile aerobic base you are not using. Zone 2 is the base that everything else sits on, it is the lowest-impact run you can do at 250 lb, and it is the perfect partner to eighteen minutes of gauntlet on six hours of sleep. The difficulty here is entirely psychological, which is precisely why it has been skipped seven or eight times running. Run it easy. That's the whole assignment.

blocks.title: CORE · ROTATION UNDER LOAD
blocks.meta: ~5 min · 16 kg · 3 fast rounds · the figure-8 has never been in this program
blocks.format: 3 ROUNDS · straight through, ~20s rest between rounds
blocks.workRest: Short and to the point. Your last three core blocks were frontal plane, overhead anti-extension, and direct flexion — the gap is loaded rotation moving through the legs, and the figure-8 is the cleanest way to train it. Keep the bell moving smoothly; this is rhythm work, not a strength test.

items.name: Figure-8 to Hold ×6/side (WILDCARD)
items.detail: 16 kg · NEW — this has never appeared in your log. Stand in a wide athletic stance, hinge slightly, and pass the bell from one hand to the other BEHIND and between your legs in a figure-8 pattern. Every second pass, catch it in front and pull it into a one-second hold at chest height before continuing. Six passes each side. Your midline is resisting the bell trying to twist you the whole time, and your grip has to catch a moving weight repeatedly — which after the gauntlet is the point.

items.name: Hollow Rock ×12
items.detail: bodyweight · flat on your back, low back PRESSED into the floor, arms overhead, legs straight and just off the ground. Rock as one rigid piece from the shoulders. If the low back lifts off the floor, tuck the knees in until it doesn't. Twelve controlled reps, not twelve flails.

blocks.text: Loaded rotation and anti-extension in five minutes. The figure-8 is your wildcard and it does three jobs at once — it moves load across your body, it forces your midline to refuse the twist, and it makes your grip catch a moving bell over and over, which is the exact quality that gave out on you Monday. Three rounds and you're done.

blocks.title: COOLDOWN
blocks.meta: ~3 min · hips and T-spine from the get-ups, forearms from six stations of one-bell work
blocks.text: Walk 60s at 3.0, 0%. Then: half-kneeling hip flexor 30s/side (the get-ups loaded those) · standing hamstring stretch 30s/side · overhead lat and tricep stretch 30s/side · doorway or floor pec stretch 30s/side · forearm and wrist flexor stretch 30s each direction — you held one bell for every station today · 5 slow nasal breaths. Report back with THREE things and nothing else: how many full rounds of the gauntlet you finished out of 4, which station started breaking down first, and whether you actually held the Zone 2 easy or let it drift up. Those three tell me whether the next gauntlet adds a station or adds load, and whether Zone 2 earns a permanent slot in your run rotation. Incline is queued for your next run day.

timer.emomUnit: No EMOM today. Block 1 is an 18-minute COUNTDOWN — cycle the six stations continuously and count ROUNDS (target 4), resting 45–60s only at the end of a full round. Block 2 is an 18-minute COUNTDOWN at one steady speed. Block 3 is 3 rounds by feel.
